title: Causal inference in two-sided randomization designs: factorial regression, two-way clustering, and covariate adjustment
abstract: arXiv:2609.22761v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: We study randomized experiments involving two interacting populations, such as buyers and sellers in a marketplace. In the two-sided experiments we consider, we randomize the two populations separately and independently. For a pair consisting of one member from each population, the two assignments jointly determine one of four exposure conditions. Under a local interference assumption, we consider a broad class of linear estimands, including total, interaction, and buyer- and seller-side spillover effects. Our first main result establishes that researchers can estimate these effects using ordinary least squares and conduct asymptotically valid design-based inference using the conventional two-way cluster-robust variance estimator, clustered at the buyers' and sellers' levels. Our second main result develops a sharper variance estimator for a single linear estimand that better preserves dependence within the buyer and seller dimensions an

translated_title: 双边随机化设计中的因果推断：因子回归、双向聚类与协变量调整
translated_abstract: 我们研究涉及两个相互作用的群体的随机实验，例如市场平台中的买家和卖家。在我们所考虑的双边实验中，我们对这两个群体分别独立地进行随机化。对于由每个群体中各一名成员组成的配对，两个分配结果共同决定了四种暴露条件之一。在局部干扰假设下，我们考虑了一类广泛的线性估计对象，包括总效应、交互效应以及买家侧和卖家侧的溢出效应。我们的第一个主要结果证明了研究人员可以使用普通最小二乘法（OLS）来估计这些效应，并使用在买家和卖家层面聚类的传统双向聚类稳健方差估计量进行渐近有效的设计基础推断。我们的第二个主要结果为单个线性估计对象开发了一种更精确的方差估计量，它能更好地保留买家和卖家维度内部的依赖性。
tldr: 该论文针对买家与卖家等双边随机化实验，证明了使用普通最小二乘法配合传统的双向聚类稳健方差估计量，即可对总效应、交互效应及买卖双方溢出效应等线性估计对象进行渐近有效的设计推断，并提出了一种能更好保留买家与卖家维度内依赖性的更精确方差估计量。
en_tdlr: For two-sided randomized experiments involving interacting populations such as buyers and sellers, this paper establishes that OLS combined with the conventional two-way cluster-robust variance estimator yields asymptotically valid design-based inference for a broad class of linear estimands (including total, interaction, and spillover effects), and develops a sharper variance estimator that better preserves dependence within the buyer and seller dimensions.
